payload.as_is: Pain 1 - one working directory serializes everything: only ONE iteration can be open per worktree (SE-C-031 enforces it), so i8 waits for i5 which waited for i4; the owner asked for parallel today and the honest answer was 'not until worktrees exist' (witness: today's chat, the owner's parallel ask deferred by ruling). Pain 2 - no isolation between concurrent edit streams: if two work streams ran in one tree, engine edits and ledger mints would interleave on the same files with no boundary; the fence and CAS protect against clobbering but not against semantic mixing (witness: the i4 session itself - board fixes rode into gate commits because everything shares one tree; the M8 commit carried a bin/ fix that belonged to no chunk). Pain 3 - merges carry no honesty marks: v2 has never merged two lines of work; when it does, git resolves textually and NOTHING marks the ledger nodes both sides touched - the suspect system exists as a concept (uc-4's across-iterations pass line, edges.ts suspect directions) but no merge writes suspect marks (witness: uc-4's unpaid pass line, carried since i2). Pain 4 - the plan knows no dependencies: plan.json gained depends_on (i10 uses it) but nothing READS it - no engine check stops a dependent iteration from firing early, and nothing declares two iterations independent enough to fire together (witness: plan.json today - depends_on only on i10, unenforced). Pain 5 - the board assumes one root: state.json is projected from the single boot root; a second worktree would be invisible - no tab, no machine frame, no offer surface (witness: bin/se-board.ts, single --root arg; agents list hardcodes mallard).
